# deploy/ — production deploy bundle for {{SERVICE_NAME}}

Standalone, agent-free deploy scripts generated by the
`bentoml-deploy-scriptgen` skill. Python >= 3.9 plus PyYAML; external tools
(`bentoml`, `docker`, `kubectl`, `aws`) are invoked via subprocess and validated
by preflight checks before anything is mutated.

**`config.yml` is the only file you edit.** Do not edit `deploy.py` or anything
under `_internal/`. The Kubernetes manifests are **rendered from `config.yml`
on every run** and piped straight to `kubectl apply` — there is no hand-owned
YAML to keep in sync. If `config.yml` cannot express what you need, regenerate
the bundle with the skill (or, as a last resort, take ownership of the YAML with
`kubernetes.manifests_dir` — see below).

PyYAML is the bundle's one third-party requirement (the standard library has no
YAML parser). The `bentoml` package already depends on it, so any machine that
can build is fine; a deploy-only environment needs `pip install pyyaml`.
Preflight reports it as `common.pyyaml`.

## Usage

```bash
# Preflight only — safe anywhere, changes nothing:
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --check-only

# Same, but without needing cluster/registry credentials (CI PR gate):
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --check-only --local-only

# Show exactly what would be applied (writes deploy/rendered/, applies nothing):
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --render-only

# Full pipeline: build the Bento, containerize, push, render, apply, verify.
# The image tag defaults to the project's short git SHA:
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s

# Re-running at the same git SHA is idempotent: the already-built bento is
# reused. If you force a REBUILD at the same tag (bentoml delete + re-run),
# the registry tag is reassigned to a new digest, the previous image stays
# as an untagged leftover, and nodes that cached the old digest keep it
# under imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent — prefer a new commit (new tag) over
# rebuilding an existing one.

# Deploy an already-pushed image (no build), e.g. for rollback:
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --skip-build \
    --image {{IMAGE_REGISTRY}}/{{IMAGE_REPOSITORY}}:<tag>

# EC2: the same pipeline, deployed onto the instances in ec2.hosts
# (export the values for every name in ec2.env_names first):
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target ec2 --check-only   # probes every host over SSH
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target ec2
```

### Flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--target {k8s,ec2}` | Required. Targets not generated into this bundle exit with code 2. |
| `--check-only` | Run every applicable preflight check in one aggregated pass and exit; nothing is changed. |
| `--local-only` | With `--check-only`: only checks that need no cluster or registry connectivity (config validity, rendering, tool presence). Skipped checks are listed in the summary's `skipped_checks`. |
| `--render-only [DIR]` | k8s only. Render the manifests from `config.yml` into `DIR` (default `deploy/rendered/`) and exit 0 **without touching the cluster** — nothing is built, applied, or contacted. The review/diff/GitOps path; also the migration path to `kubernetes.manifests_dir`. Cannot be combined with `--check-only` (they are separate modes; run them one after the other). |
| `--skip-build` | Skip build/containerize/push (and their preflights); deploy an existing image. Preflight then verifies the image actually exists in the registry (ECR `describe-images`, or `docker manifest inspect`) so a typo cannot burn the rollout timeout. |
| `--image REF` | Full image reference to deploy (overrides config registry/repository and the tag). |
| `--version TAG` | Image tag to build and deploy. Default: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` of the project (a non-git project fails preflight with instructions). |
| `--no-verify` | Skip the post-deploy `/readyz` + inference verification. |
| `--config PATH` | Alternate config file (default: `config.yml` next to `deploy.py`). |
| `--output-json PATH` | Also write the machine-readable summary to a file. |

Environment overrides (lower precedence than flags): `BENTOML_DEPLOY_IMAGE`,
`BENTOML_DEPLOY_VERSION`, `BENTOML_DEPLOY_K8S_CONTEXT`,
`BENTOML_DEPLOY_K8S_NAMESPACE`, `BENTOML_DEPLOY_EC2_HOSTS`
(comma-separated, overrides `ec2.hosts`).

Secrets are **never** read from the config or written to disk. AWS/ECR
credentials come from the ambient AWS environment (`AWS_PROFILE`,
`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or SSO); docker registry logins
come from `docker login`; cluster access comes from your kubeconfig.

### Exit codes

`0` ok · `1` generic · `2` config error · `3` preflight failure ·
`4` build/containerize · `5` push · `6` deploy · `7` verify.

The **last line of stdout is always a JSON summary** (all progress logging
goes to stderr), e.g.:

```json
{"schema": "bentoml-deploy-summary/v1", "ok": true, "exit_code": 0, "target": "k8s", "action": "deploy", "image": "...", "version": "...", "stages": [...], "skipped_checks": [...], "error": null, ...}
```

`action` is `deploy`, `check-only`, or `render-only`. `stages` carries the
pipeline steps (`preflight`, `build`, `containerize`, `push`, `deploy`,
`verify`, or the single `render` stage under `--render-only`) plus one entry per
unit of work inside a step:

- `k8s.apply` — the `kubectl apply` itself, with a `detail` naming where the
  YAML came from: `rendered N object(s) from config.yml`, or `applied N file(s)
  from <dir> VERBATIM (kubernetes.manifests_dir) — the image refs in those files
  are what runs; this run's image (…) was NOT substituted`;
- `k8s.rollout[<slug>]` — one per BentoML service, in rollout order;
- `ec2.deploy[<host>]` / `ec2.verify[<host>]` — one per host (ec2).

In CI: `python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s | tail -n 1 > summary.json`.
One caveat: command-line usage errors (unknown flag, missing `--target`) are
rejected by the argument parser itself — those exit 2 **without** a JSON
summary, because parsing happens before the summary machinery starts.

## config.yml

Every key, with its default. Anything marked *derived* is computed for you and
must not be maintained by hand. Validation failures exit 2 and name the exact
path, e.g. `services.Gateway.expose.node_port`.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `bentoml-deploy-config/v3` | Config schema. A v1/v2 config (the old `deploy.config.json`) is rejected with migration instructions — there is no in-place upgrade. |
| `project.dir` | `..` | BentoML project root, resolved **relative to the config file itself** (`deploy/config.yml` here, hence `..`). |
| `project.service` | `null` | `bentoml build` target as `module:Class`. Required when `service.py` defines several services. |
| `project.name` | — | Bento name. Names the ec2 container and the `app.kubernetes.io/part-of` label on every rendered object. |
| `image.registry` | `""` | Registry host (`…dkr.ecr.…amazonaws.com`, `ghcr.io`, `docker.io`). `""` for a local-only image. |
| `image.repository` | — | Repository/name inside the registry. |
| `image.registry_type` | `generic` | `ecr` (login + describe-or-create the repo), `generic` (you keep `docker login` valid), `none` (nothing pushed; requires `local_image_preloaded: true`). |
| `image.platform` | `null` | `"linux/amd64"` when cluster nodes are amd64 and builds may run on arm64. Preflight then checks buildx. |
| `image.ecr_region` | `null` | Derived from the registry host when null. |
| `image.local_image_preloaded` | `false` | Acknowledgement that a `registry_type: none` image is already loaded onto the nodes. **Required true** with `registry_type: none`. |
| `kubernetes.context` | — | kubectl context; every kubectl call passes `--context` explicitly. |
| `kubernetes.namespace` | — | Must already exist. Nothing renders a Namespace object and the script never creates one; preflight fails with the `kubectl create namespace` line. |
| `kubernetes.image_pull_secret` | `null` | Existing pull secret name; rendered as `imagePullSecrets` on every pod. |
| `kubernetes.rollout_timeout_seconds` | `900` | Per-Deployment `rollout status` budget. Keep it **above** `probes.startup_failure_threshold` x 10 s. |
| `kubernetes.local_port` | `3130` | Verification port-forward. `local_port + 1` carries the dependency `/metrics` scrapes, so keep both free. |
| `kubernetes.extra_labels` | `{}` | Extra labels merged onto every rendered object. Quoted string values. The `app.kubernetes.io/*` labels are managed by the renderer and win. |
| `kubernetes.manifests_dir` | `null` | **Escape hatch.** When set, rendering is skipped and that directory's YAML is applied **verbatim**, image ref included (see below). |
| `services.<Name>` | — | One block per BentoML service; the key is the service name **exactly** as the bento declares it (`--service-name` and dependency lookup both key on it). |
| `services.<Name>.entry` | `false` | Exactly one service must be `true`: the bento's entry service, the only one that may be exposed and the only one verification targets. |
| `services.<Name>.slug` | *derived* | Kubernetes object name and in-cluster hostname. Defaults to the service name snake_cased with `_`→`-`; must be a unique DNS-1035 label. |
| `services.<Name>.depends` | `[]` | BentoML service names this one calls directly. Drives the rollout order and `BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS` — both *derived*. |
| `services.<Name>.replicas` | `1` | Fixed pod count. Omitted from the Deployment when `autoscaling.enabled`. |
| `services.<Name>.resources.requests` / `.limits` | `{}` | Kubernetes quantities as **quoted strings** (`cpu: "1"`, not `cpu: 1`). Always set all four: `@bentoml.service(resources={"cpu","memory"})` is **inert** in open-source BentoML, so nothing else constrains the pod. GPUs are limits-only: `nvidia.com/gpu: "1"`. |
| `services.<Name>.env` | `{}` | Plain, non-secret env vars. Quoted string values. |
| `services.<Name>.env_from_secrets` | `[]` | Existing Secret names → `envFrom.secretRef`. **No static check can see inside a Secret**: a `BENTOML_RUNNER_MAP` (or `BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS`) key in one of these Secrets reaches the pod and silently overrides the wiring — the runner-map trap below with no warning anywhere. Keep these Secrets to credentials. |
| `services.<Name>.config_overrides` | `{}` | **Bare** per-service BentoML config (`{workers: 2, traffic: {timeout: 120}}`). The renderer nests it under `{"services": {"<Name>": …}}` and emits `BENTOML_CONFIG_OVERRIDES` as compact JSON — that per-service form beats the `@bentoml.service(...)` decorator, a global one loses to it. Ignored when you set `BENTOML_CONFIG_OVERRIDES` yourself in `env` (raw wins). |
| `services.<Name>.node_selector` | `{}` | Node pinning. Quoted string values. |
| `services.<Name>.tolerations` | `[]` | Verbatim Kubernetes tolerations. |
| `services.<Name>.probes.startup_failure_threshold` | `60` | Startup budget = this x `periodSeconds: 10` (so 60 → 10 min of model loading). |
| `services.<Name>.probes.readiness_timeout_seconds` | `6` | `timeoutSeconds` on the `/readyz` probes. **6 is a floor, enforced:** BentoML gives a dependency a hard-coded 5 s budget when `/readyz` fans out, so a lower timeout makes the kubelet hang up first and the pod stays permanently unready. Raise it for deep chains; never lower it. |
| `services.<Name>.autoscaling.enabled` | `false` | `true` renders an HPA **and** omits `spec.replicas` (a declared count and an HPA fight on every apply). |
| `services.<Name>.autoscaling.min_replicas` / `max_replicas` | `1` / `5` | HPA bounds (no scale-to-zero). |
| `services.<Name>.autoscaling.metric` | `cpu` | `cpu` = `Resource/cpu averageUtilization` (stock metrics-server; requires `requests.cpu`, which is enforced). `concurrency` = `Pods` metric on `bentoml_service_request_in_progress`, which needs a custom-metrics adapter. |
| `services.<Name>.autoscaling.target` | `70` | % of requested CPU, or in-flight requests per pod. |
| `services.<Name>.expose` | ClusterIP | **Entry service only** (rejected elsewhere). `type`: `ClusterIP`/`NodePort`/`LoadBalancer`; `node_port` 30000–32767, only with `type: NodePort`; `annotations` for cloud LBs. |
| `services.<Name>.ingress` | disabled | **Entry service only.** `enabled`, `class_name`, `host` (required when enabled), `tls_secret`, `annotations`. |
| `verify.readyz_timeout_seconds` | `600` | How long `/readyz` may take to return 200 after the rollouts finish. |
| `verify.dependency_metrics` | `true` | Prove each dependency actually served a request (see below). |
| `verify.inference.path` / `.body` / `.expect_substring` / `.timeout_seconds` | — / — / `null` / `60` | Smoke test against the entry service; `body` is native YAML. `inference: null` skips it. |
| `ec2.*` | — | See the ec2 chapter: `hosts`, `ssh_user`, `ssh_key_path`, `container_name`, `host_port`, `env_names`, `registry_auth`, `verify_via`, `local_tunnel_port`. |

Unknown keys are warned about (typo protection), not ignored silently.

## How the k8s deploy works

**One Deployment + one Service per BentoML service**, plus an HPA per service
with `autoscaling.enabled` and one Ingress for the entry service when
`ingress.enabled`. A single-service bento degenerates to exactly one
Deployment + Service. Each run:

1. **Render from `config.yml`, in memory.** The renderer writes this run's image
   ref straight into every Deployment (there is no image sentinel any more),
   derives `BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS` from `depends`, and pipes the whole set to
   `kubectl apply -n <namespace> -f -`. Nothing is written to disk; re-applying
   the full set (rather than `kubectl set image`) reconciles drift and recreates
   objects that were deleted. Output is deterministic, so
   `--render-only` diffs are meaningful.
2. **Wait for every rollout, in the derived order** — a topological sort of
   `depends`, deepest dependencies first and the entry service last, each with
   its own `kubectl rollout status --timeout=kubernetes.rollout_timeout_seconds`.
   The order is load-bearing: a caller's `/readyz` fans out to its dependencies,
   so it stays unready (503) until they answer. The run **fails fast** — the
   first failing rollout aborts it and the error names the offending BentoML
   service and Deployment.
3. **Verify through the entry service.** `/readyz` plus the configured inference
   request go through a port-forward to `svc/<entry slug>` on
   `kubernetes.local_port` (the probe is only trusted while the port-forward
   process is alive and bound). The public HTTP API is only spoken by the entry
   service; dependency Services stay ClusterIP because inter-service payloads
   are `application/vnd.bentoml+pickle`.
4. **Prove the dependencies were actually called** (multi-service bentos,
   `verify.dependency_metrics`, default `true`). A green `/readyz` and a correct
   inference answer do **not** imply the dependency pods did anything: if a
   caller's `BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS` does not name a dependency exactly as the
   bento declares it, BentoML instantiates that dependency **in-process** — with
   no log line — so that pod loads every model itself, answers correctly, and
   reports ready while the dependency pods idle. Readiness cannot catch it
   either: `/readyz` only fans out to dependencies that are remote proxies, so
   an in-process one is skipped and readiness is trivially true. So each
   dependency's own `bentoml_service_request_total` is sampled (through a
   short-lived port-forward to its ClusterIP Service, on `local_port + 1`)
   before and after the inference request, and verify fails (exit 7) unless it
   moved. Samples for health endpoints are excluded, so kubelet probes and the
   readiness fan-out cannot be mistaken for an inference call; scraping
   `/metrics` is itself uninstrumented, so measuring does not disturb the
   measurement.

Per-service outcomes appear in the summary's `stages` as `k8s.rollout[<slug>]` —
one per service, in rollout order. After a failure, the services that were never
reached are recorded with `"ok": false` and `"detail": "not attempted (fail-fast
after an earlier service's rollout failed)"`, so CI can tell "broken" from
"never tried".

### Review before applying: `--render-only`

```bash
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --render-only            # -> deploy/rendered/
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --render-only /tmp/next  # -> any directory
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --render-only --version review   # no git needed
```

**It needs an image reference**, because a rendered Deployment carries a
concrete one: `--image REF`, or `--version TAG` (combined with
`image.registry`/`image.repository`), or a git checkout — the default tag is
`git rev-parse --short HEAD` of `project.dir`, so outside a git repo the run
fails with exit 2 telling you to pass one. Nothing is built either way; the ref
is only written into the YAML.

It writes one file per object (`<slug>-deployment.yaml`,
`<slug>-service.yaml`, `<slug>-hpa.yaml`, `ingress.yaml`) — the same names and
shapes the interactive `bentoml-k8s-deploy` skill renders from the same
`config.yml` — prints the
rollout order it derived, and exits 0 without contacting the cluster, building
anything, or applying anything. Use it to:

- **review a config change**: render before and after and `diff -r` the two
  directories (the output is deterministic — stable key order, sorted maps);
- **dry-run against the API server**:
  `kubectl --context {{K8S_CONTEXT}} apply --dry-run=server -f deploy/rendered`;
- **feed GitOps**: commit the rendered directory, or hand it to Argo CD/Flux.
  The rendered Deployments carry a **concrete** image ref (the resolved tag), so
  re-render on every release, or pass `--image`/`--version` explicitly.

`deploy/rendered/` is generated output: safe to delete, re-created from
`config.yml` on demand, and never read by the deploy path (which renders in
memory) — `.gitignore` it unless you are deliberately committing manifests for
GitOps.

Re-rendering **prunes** its own stale files: a `<slug>-deployment.yaml`,
`<slug>-service.yaml`, `<slug>-hpa.yaml` or `ingress.yaml` that no longer
corresponds to the config (a renamed slug, a deleted service, autoscaling turned
off) is deleted and the removal is logged. That is deliberate rather than
tidiness: left behind, `kubectl apply -f <dir>` — or a GitOps controller watching
the directory — re-creates the orphaned Deployment and Service on the next
apply, and its pods keep serving. Files the renderer does not own (a sidecar
patch, a kustomization, a README) are never touched, but they *are* listed with a
warning, because applying the directory applies them too.

Every rendered object carries `app.kubernetes.io/name: <slug>` (also the pod
selector), `app.kubernetes.io/component: <BentoML service name>`,
`app.kubernetes.io/part-of: <bento name>` and
`app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: bentoml-k8s-deploy`, plus
`kubernetes.extra_labels`. That `managed-by` value is shared with the
interactive `bentoml-k8s-deploy` skill on purpose: both render the same shapes
from the same `config.yml`, so
`kubectl get all -l app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=bentoml-k8s-deploy` finds the
whole deployment however it was applied, and switching between them rewrites
nothing.

### Escape hatch: `kubernetes.manifests_dir`

Set it (a path relative to `deploy/`) when you have genuinely outgrown
`config.yml` — a sidecar, a PVC, a ServiceMonitor, an init container. Then:

- rendering is **skipped**; every `*.yaml`/`*.yml` in that directory is applied
  **verbatim**, in name order, in one pass. Nothing is substituted — **including
  the image reference**: those files pin whatever tag they carry, so this run's
  built/passed ref does not reach the pods unless the files name it. The deploy
  log and the `k8s.apply` stage's `detail` say so on every run, and preflight
  warns when the pinned refs differ from the resolved image;
- `config.yml`'s `services:` blocks still drive the rollout order, the
  verification target, and the wiring checks — but no longer the workload shape;
- `--render-only` refuses to run (there is nothing to render) and says so.

Migration path: `--render-only DIR`, commit `DIR`, then point
`kubernetes.manifests_dir` at it; from then on edit the tag per build, or
**unset `manifests_dir` again to re-render** — `--render-only` deliberately
refuses while the key is set, so a re-render is: unset, render, set it back
(and re-apply your own edits on top, which is why small diffs are worth
keeping). Going back is just unsetting the key. The trade-off is real: from then on
*you* own the labels, probes, dependency wiring, namespaces **and image tags** in
that YAML, and adding a BentoML service means editing both the config and the
manifests.

This is also the answer for the knobs `config.yml` deliberately does not have —
`path_prefix` probe paths, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, liveness timings,
`imagePullPolicy`, `revisionHistoryLimit`, HPA `behavior` windows,
affinity/`topologySpreadConstraints`, volumes, sidecars, PodDisruptionBudgets.
They are `manifests_dir` territory on purpose; the config gains no key for them.

### What preflight checks — and the shift since manifests became rendered

Preflight always runs as **one aggregated pass**: every applicable check runs,
and a single exit 3 reports all failures together.

Credential-free (so `--check-only --local-only` runs them): `common.pyyaml`,
`common.python-version`, `common.git-repo`, `build.*`, `k8s.kubectl-cli`, plus

- `k8s.render` — renders the manifests exactly as the deploy would and parses
  every document, so a config that cannot render fails before anything is built;
- `k8s.rollout-plan` — prints the derived rollout order and every
  `BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS` value, so a wrong `depends:` is visible up front.

Needing the cluster: `k8s.context-reachable`, `k8s.rbac-create-deployment`,
`k8s.namespace`, `k8s.image-pull-secret`.

**The checks that used to police hand-written YAML are gone from the rendering
path — because they are now impossible to fail, not because coverage was
dropped.** Each of the five moved from "checked afterwards" to "cannot happen":

| Old check | Why it cannot fail now |
|---|---|
| image sentinel present, nothing pinned | The renderer writes the run's image ref straight into every Deployment; there is no file that could pin a stale tag. |
| every object declares the configured namespace | The renderer stamps `metadata.namespace` from `kubernetes.namespace` on every object. |
| each dependency wired via `BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS`, no runner map | Derived from `depends` (validated: targets exist, no cycles, no duplicate keys). A runner map is emitted by nothing, ever — and a runner map you put in `env` yourself is a config error. The one way to take over the wiring is `env: {BENTOML_SERVE_DEPENDS: …}`, which **replaces** the derived value; the loader then applies the same rules to your string (one `=` per pair, no commas, http(s) URLs, and every name in `depends` covered — a misspelled name fails with a path) and `--check-only` prints the raw value, marked `[raw]`, instead of the derived one that will not be emitted. |
| non-entry Services are ClusterIP with no nodePort | Non-entry Services are rendered ClusterIP unconditionally, and `expose`/`ingress` on a non-entry service is a **config error** (exit 2). |
| no `spec.replicas` next to an HPA | `spec.replicas` is omitted whenever the same service's HPA is rendered. |

The equivalents stay **fully active** when `kubernetes.manifests_dir` is set —
that YAML is hand-owned, so `k8s.manifests`, `k8s.serve-depends` and
`k8s.service-exposure` check the same properties (namespace consistency,
dependency wiring, no runner map, non-entry ClusterIP, no `replicas:` beside an
HPA, and an `image:` line in every Deployment — verbatim, so a drifting tag is a
warning naming both refs) plus one
`<slug>-deployment.yaml` + `<slug>-service.yaml` per configured service, and no
leftover `{{PLACEHOLDER}}`). The rest of the invariants moved *into config
validation*, where the error can name your line: exactly one `entry: true`,
`depends` targets that exist, no dependency cycles, unique DNS-1035 slugs,
quantities that are quoted strings, a NodePort in range and only with
`type: NodePort`, the readiness-timeout floor, `registry_type: none` requiring
`local_image_preloaded`, no duplicate YAML keys (which YAML itself resolves
last-wins in silence), a `manifests_dir` that exists, JSON-serializable
`verify.inference.body` / `config_overrides` / `tolerations` (checked at load,
not when the smoke test POSTs after the cluster was already changed), and no
runner-map env var.

One hole no check can close: `env_from_secrets` mounts whole Secrets, and a
`BENTOML_RUNNER_MAP` key inside one reaches the pod unseen. Nothing outside the
cluster can read those values — keep those Secrets to credentials.

### Notes on specific config keys

- `services:` — adding or removing a BentoML service is a **one-file** change
  now: add its block, list it in the caller's `depends`, re-run. The rollout
  order, the dependency URLs, the labels and the selectors all follow.
- `verify.dependency_metrics` (default `true`) — the dependency-call proof
  described above. Set it to `false` only when a dependency is deliberately
  **not** on the code path of `verify.inference.path` (then it legitimately
  receives no request); the run warns loudly that it can no longer tell a
  working split from an in-process fallback. It also needs `local_port + 1`
  free and `/metrics` reachable on the dependencies.
- `kubernetes.rollout_timeout_seconds` (default `900`) — deliberately **larger**
  than the rendered startup budget (`probes.startup_failure_threshold: 60` x
  `periodSeconds: 10` = 600 s). With the two equal, a pod that legitimately uses
  its whole startup budget loses the race and the rollout is declared failed at
  the moment it would have succeeded. Keep the slack if you raise the probe
  budget for slow model loads.
- `autoscaling` — the HPA is rendered only while `enabled: true`. Setting it
  back to `false` stops rendering the HPA but does **not** delete the
  HorizontalPodAutoscaler already in the cluster: `kubectl delete hpa <slug>`.
  (The reverse — `enabled: true` — takes effect on the next deploy, and that
  service's `replicas:` stops being applied at the same moment.)
- `expose.node_port` — set it (30000–32767) for a stable NodePort URL; unset
  (`null`) lets the cluster allocate, and `kubectl apply` preserves whatever it
  already allocated. Rejected on a `ClusterIP` service, and rejected outright on
  a non-entry service.
- `image.registry_type: "none"` — nothing is pushed; you must load the image into
  the cluster nodes yourself (`minikube image load` / `kind load docker-image`)
  and acknowledge with `local_image_preloaded: true` — which the config loader
  now requires, so a forgotten load fails in milliseconds instead of dying in
  ImagePullBackOff after the whole rollout timeout.
- `kubernetes.image_pull_secret` — preflight checks the secret exists and, for
  ECR, warns when it is older than 11 h (tokens expire after 12 h). Refresh by
  **deleting and recreating** the secret — `kubectl apply` keeps the original
  creationTimestamp, so an applied-over secret still looks old. The age check is
  a heuristic only: it cannot detect a freshly created secret that embeds an
  already-expired token.
- `services.<Name>.config_overrides` — the runtime retuning knob (workers,
  `traffic.timeout`, `runner_probe`) that needs no image rebuild. Two traps: it
  only beats the decorator **under the service's own name**, and a dependency's
  client timeout is read from the **caller's** config, so raising a dependency's
  `traffic.timeout` must be done in both blocks.

### Known upstream noise

`bentoml containerize` (1.4.x) emits a few
`UserWarning: The parameter --quiet is used more than once` lines from click on
every invocation — an upstream duplicate-option declaration, not a problem with
this bundle or your project. It lands in the build stage's stderr on every run;
ignore it.

## How the ec2 deploy works

`--target ec2` deploys the image onto the **existing** instances listed in
`ec2.hosts` — the script never provisions EC2 (use the interactive
`bentoml-ec2-deploy` skill to create instances first). Hosts are deployed
and verified sequentially and **fail fast**: the first failing host aborts
the run, and per-host outcomes appear in the summary's `stages` as
`ec2.deploy[<host>]` / `ec2.verify[<host>]` (unattempted hosts are marked).
Every remote docker command runs under `sudo` over key-based SSH
(`ec2.ssh_key_path`, BatchMode — nothing may prompt). Per host:

1. **Registry login** — with `registry_auth: "ecr-token-over-ssh"`, the
   local AWS credentials mint a fresh ECR token (`aws ecr
   get-login-password`, region taken from the image ref) and pipe it over
   the SSH channel's stdin into `sudo docker login --password-stdin`; the
   token never touches a file or a command line. With `"preauthed"` the
   instances must already be able to pull (instance profile, or a
   `docker login` you keep fresh yourself — ECR tokens expire after 12 h).
2. `sudo docker pull <image>`
3. `sudo docker rm -f <container_name>` (idempotent redeploy), then
   `sudo docker run -d --name <container_name> --restart unless-stopped
   -p <host_port>:3000 ... <image>`
4. Wait 3 s, then require `docker ps` to report the container **Up** — a
   crash-looping container still shows `Up` at t=0, so the wait is
   load-bearing.
5. **Verify** `/readyz` plus the configured inference request:
   - `verify_via: "tunnel"` (default) — a hardened SSH tunnel
     (`-o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes`, liveness-checked around every probe so
     a local port squatter can never fake a green result) on local port
     `ec2.local_tunnel_port`. Works even when the security group
     never exposes the host port.
   - `verify_via: "direct"` — plain HTTP to `http://<host>:<host_port>`;
     requires the security group to allow that port from the deploying
     machine. The container is re-checked over SSH first so the responder
     is known to be ours.

The ec2 target renders no manifests and ignores `services:` /
`kubernetes:` entirely.

### Secrets / runtime env vars (ec2)

`ec2.env_names` lists variable **names only** (e.g.
`["HF_TOKEN"]`). At deploy time each value is read from the deploying
process's environment — preflight fails if any is missing — transported
base64-encoded over the SSH channel's stdin, exported on the remote side,
and handed to the container with docker's value-less `-e NAME` form. Values
never appear in the config, in any file, or in any command line on either
machine (`ps` shows nothing on either end).

### Rollback (ec2)

`docker rm -f` + `run` replaces the container in place, so there is no
previous revision to undo into — a rollback is a redeploy of the previous
tag (deterministic git-SHA tags make this easy):

```bash
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target ec2 --skip-build \
    --image {{IMAGE_REGISTRY}}/{{IMAGE_REPOSITORY}}:<previous-tag>
```

Exit codes and the summary contract are unchanged (same table above).

## Rollback (k8s)

Kubernetes keeps the previous ReplicaSets — **per Deployment**, so roll back
every service the run touched, dependencies first and the entry service last
(the same order the deploy uses, for the same reason). One pair per service in
`config.yml`'s `services:`:

```bash
# dependencies first:
kubectl --context {{K8S_CONTEXT}} -n {{NAMESPACE}} rollout undo deployment/{{DEP_SERVICE_SLUG}}
kubectl --context {{K8S_CONTEXT}} -n {{NAMESPACE}} rollout status deployment/{{DEP_SERVICE_SLUG}}
# entry service last:
kubectl --context {{K8S_CONTEXT}} -n {{NAMESPACE}} rollout undo deployment/{{ENTRY_SERVICE_SLUG}}
kubectl --context {{K8S_CONTEXT}} -n {{NAMESPACE}} rollout status deployment/{{ENTRY_SERVICE_SLUG}}
```

A failed deploy prints exactly this list for your services (plus the
`get pods` / `describe` / `logs` commands for each one) in its error hint, so
you never have to reconstruct it by hand.

Or redeploy a known-good tag explicitly (deterministic tags make this easy):

```bash
python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --skip-build \
    --image {{IMAGE_REGISTRY}}/{{IMAGE_REPOSITORY}}:<previous-tag>
```

Note that a rollback of the **image** is not a rollback of the **config**: the
manifests are rendered from `config.yml` at your current checkout, so revert the
config change too (that is one more reason to commit `config.yml`, and to keep
`--render-only` diffs in review).

## CI/CD

The bundle is designed to be the *entire* deploy step of a pipeline: exit
codes 0..7 tell CI what failed, and the last stdout line is the JSON
summary (`... | tail -n 1 > summary.json`, or `--output-json`). Three
patterns cover everything:

- **PR gate**: `--check-only --local-only` — config validity, rendering,
  tool presence. Needs **no** credentials, cluster, or registry, so it is
  safe on any runner including fork PRs — but note it still checks that the
  target's CLI tools are **on PATH** (docker always; the AWS CLI v2 for
  ECR; kubectl for k8s; ssh for ec2), so the job must install them.
- **Manifest diff in review** (optional, k8s): `--render-only` on the PR and
  on the base commit, then `diff -r` the two directories and post the result —
  reviewers see the Kubernetes change a `config.yml` edit produces.
- **Deploy on main**: the full run. The runner needs Python >= 3.9, PyYAML, the
  `bentoml` CLI, docker (build/containerize/push), the AWS CLI v2 for
  ECR / EC2-with-ECR, and target-specific access (kubeconfig, SSH key, or
  an AWS role).

Any job that does **not** `pip install bentoml` (a `--skip-build` deploy, a
render-only diff job) must `pip install pyyaml` — that is the config parser.

Secrets wiring (nothing is ever read from the config or written into the
repo):

| Secret | Used by | How it reaches the script |
|---|---|---|
| AWS role (OIDC, preferred) or access keys | ECR push; ec2 with `ecr-token-over-ssh` | ambient AWS env — `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` on GitHub, `AWS_ROLE_ARN` + `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` on GitLab |
| SSH private key | ec2 | written by the job to the path in `ec2.ssh_key_path`, mode 600 |
| Runtime env values (names in `ec2.env_names`) | ec2 | exported in the job's environment |

### GitHub Actions

A complete workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`). Keep only the deploy
job(s) for the target(s) generated into this bundle. The AWS jobs use OIDC
(no long-lived keys): create one IAM role trusted by GitHub's OIDC provider
and store its ARN in the `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` repository secret.

```yaml
name: deploy

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # PR gate: no credentials, no cluster/registry connectivity — fork-safe.
  check:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: pip install "bentoml>=1.4"     # brings PyYAML with it
      - run: python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --check-only --local-only
      # one line per generated target:
      # - run: python3 deploy/deploy.py --target ec2 --check-only --local-only

  # Optional: show reviewers the manifest diff a config.yml change produces.
  render-diff:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: pip install pyyaml            # no bentoml needed to render
      - run: python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --render-only /tmp/head --version ci
      - run: git checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
      - run: python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --render-only /tmp/base --version ci
      - run: diff -ru /tmp/base /tmp/head || true

  # k8s target: OIDC -> AWS credentials -> ECR push + EKS kubeconfig.
  deploy-k8s:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write   # OIDC token for configure-aws-credentials
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: pip install "bentoml>=1.4"
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: <ecr-region>
      # the --alias must equal kubernetes.context:
      - run: aws eks update-kubeconfig --name <cluster> --alias {{K8S_CONTEXT}}
      - run: python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --output-json summary.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: deploy-summary-k8s
          path: summary.json

  # ec2 target: a plain SSH-key secret; AWS credentials are only needed for
  # ECR images (push, and registry_auth "ecr-token-over-ssh").
  deploy-ec2:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - run: pip install "bentoml>=1.4"
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: <ecr-region>
      - name: Install the SSH key
        # Write it to the exact path in ec2.ssh_key_path
        # (preflight enforces mode 600).
        env:
          EC2_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.EC2_SSH_KEY }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$EC2_SSH_KEY" > ~/.ssh/deploy_key.pem
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/deploy_key.pem
      - run: python3 deploy/deploy.py --target ec2 --output-json summary.json
        # runtime env vars named in ec2.env_names go here, e.g.:
        # env:
        #   HF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HF_TOKEN }}
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: deploy-summary-ec2
          path: summary.json
```

Notes:

- The jobs above install no CLI tools because `ubuntu-latest` runners
  already ship docker, the AWS CLI v2, and kubectl — the PR gate's
  tool-presence checks and the deploy jobs' build/containerize/push all
  work out of the box. On self-hosted runners, install whatever preflight
  reports missing (exit 3 names the tool).
- Fork PRs never reach the deploy jobs (`push` to `main` only), and the PR
  gate needs no secrets — the safe default. A trusted-PR "full preflight"
  variant is the same deploy job with `--check-only` substituted in.

### GitLab CI

The equivalent `.gitlab-ci.yml`, using GitLab's OIDC (`id_tokens`) — the
AWS CLI picks up `AWS_ROLE_ARN` + `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`
automatically. The deploy job needs a docker daemon (docker-in-docker
below, or a runner with a mounted socket) and installs the AWS CLI v2
itself (v2 is not pip-installable):

```yaml
stages: [check, deploy]

check:
  stage: check
  image: python:3.11
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
  before_script:
    # --local-only skips all connectivity checks but still verifies tool
    # PRESENCE, so the bare python image needs the target CLIs installed:
    # docker (the CLI alone satisfies the presence check), the AWS CLI v2
    # for ECR images, and kubectl for the k8s target (git and ssh already
    # ship in python:3.11).
    - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq curl unzip docker.io
    - curl -sSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip" -o /tmp/awscliv2.zip
    - unzip -q /tmp/awscliv2.zip -d /tmp && /tmp/aws/install
    - curl -sSLo /usr/local/bin/kubectl "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -sSL https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
    - chmod +x /usr/local/bin/kubectl
    - pip install "bentoml>=1.4"      # brings PyYAML with it
  script:
    - python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --check-only --local-only
    # one line per generated target:
    # - python3 deploy/deploy.py --target ec2 --check-only --local-only

deploy-k8s:
  stage: deploy
  image: python:3.11
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"
  services:
    - docker:27-dind
  id_tokens:
    GITLAB_OIDC_TOKEN:
      aud: https://gitlab.com
  variables:
    DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker:2375
    DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: ""
    AWS_ROLE_ARN: arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/<gitlab-deploy-role>
    AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE: /tmp/web-identity-token
  before_script:
    - echo "$GITLAB_OIDC_TOKEN" > "$AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE"
    - apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq curl unzip docker.io
    - curl -sSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip" -o /tmp/awscliv2.zip
    - unzip -q /tmp/awscliv2.zip -d /tmp && /tmp/aws/install
    - curl -sSLo /usr/local/bin/kubectl "https://dl.k8s.io/release/$(curl -sSL https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
    - chmod +x /usr/local/bin/kubectl
    - pip install "bentoml>=1.4"
    # the --alias must equal kubernetes.context:
    - aws eks update-kubeconfig --name <cluster> --alias {{K8S_CONTEXT}}
  script:
    - python3 deploy/deploy.py --target k8s --output-json summary.json
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths: [summary.json]
```

A deploy job that skips the build (`--skip-build --image <ref>`) does not need
`bentoml`, docker, or dind — but it **does** need `pip install pyyaml`.

For the ec2 target, swap the last `script:` line for
`--target ec2`, drop the kubectl install and the
`aws eks update-kubeconfig` line, write the SSH key from a **file-type**
CI/CD variable to the path in `ec2.ssh_key_path` with mode 600 in
`before_script`, and define any `ec2.env_names` values as masked
CI/CD variables (AWS credentials stay needed only for ECR images — push,
and `registry_auth: "ecr-token-over-ssh"`).

For the k8s target on a non-EKS cluster pulling from ECR, the image pull
secret expires every 12 h — delete and recreate it in CI before deploying
(this paragraph applies regardless of which targets this bundle carries, so
keep it when pruning).
